children: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. (NSE:ONGC) took control of the disputed CB-OS-02 offshore block from Vedanta after a court rejected Vedanta’s challenge, and applied for a petroleum lease. The company declared an interim dividend of ₹8 per share, with a total payout of ₹10,064 crore.
Previous Week Recap
ONGC Takes Control Of Block
: ONGC took control of the disputed CB-OS-02 offshore block from Vedanta on July 22, 2026, after a court rejected Vedanta’s challenge to the contract decision. ONGC applied for a petroleum lease.
FY27 Interim Dividend Declared
: ONGC declared its first FY27 interim dividend at ₹8 per share, or 160% of face value. The record date is November 12, 2026, with payment due within 30 days; total payout is ₹10,064 crore.
Venezuela Project Takeover Talks
: ONGC Videsh is in advanced talks with Venezuelan and US officials to take control of the San Cristobal and Carabobo 1 oil projects. Agreements may be completed within three to six months.
Quarterly Production Declines
: ONGC’s second-quarter crude oil output fell 5.3% year over year, while natural gas production dropped 2.3%. Reservoir issues, monsoon delays and temporary customer disruptions hampered output.
ADES Holding Rig Contracts
: ONGC awarded ADES Holding $117.2 million in contracts for two jack-up rigs. Each deal runs for three years, with operations due to start by the end of Q1 2027.
Vedanta Appeal Judgment Reserved
: Vedanta appealed the Delhi High Court ruling that enabled ONGC to take over the Cambay block. The appeal hearing is complete, with judgment reserved.
Unpaid Dividends Recovery Proposed

: • Proposed operational changes could help Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. (ONGC) recover more than $500 million in unpaid dividends. Terms for settling the outstanding dividends have not yet been agreed.
Mahanadi Offshore Facility Plan
: ONGC, BP and Reliance are discussing a proposed $1 billion shared offshore facility in the Mahanadi basin to develop and transport gas and condensate. The plan remains at an early stage.
Elara Reiterates Buy Rating
: Elara Capital reiterated its Buy rating on ONGC with a ₹320 target. Key risks include crude below $70 a barrel, KG-98/2 reservoir issues, losses at HPCL and OPaL, and adverse arbitration outcomes.
CLSA Maintains Outperform Rating
: CLSA kept its “High Conviction Outperform” rating and ₹405 target for ONGC. Quarterly standalone profit missed its estimate, while EBITDA and core pre-tax profit beat forecasts.
